subject: maths
title: Finding Sides & Angles
welcome_lead: Now you'll calculate — use sin, cos, tan to find unknown sides, and inverse trig to find unknown angles.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths Trigonometry — finding unknown sides and angles in right-angled triangles using SOH-CAH-TOA and inverse trig.
final_note: You can find unknown sides with sin/cos/tan, and unknown angles with sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹.

concepts.def: O = H × sin θ (when H and θ are known).
A = H × cos θ (when H and θ are known).
H = O ÷ sin θ, or H = A ÷ cos θ.
Reverses sin to give back the angle θ.
Reverses cos to give back the angle θ.
Reverses tan to give back the angle θ.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Got the angle and one side? Pick the ratio that links what you know to what you want.

Example: angle = 30°, hypotenuse = 10. Find the opposite side.

Using SOH: sin 30° = O/10 → O = 10 × sin 30° = 10 × 0.5 = 5.

Example 2: angle = 60°, adjacent = 4. Find the opposite.

Using TOA: tan 60° = O/4 → O = 4 × tan 60° ≈ 4 × 1.732 ≈ 6.93.

When the unknown is on the bottom of the fraction, flip the formula.

Example: angle = 30°, opposite = 7. Find the hypotenuse.

sin 30° = 7/H → H = 7 ÷ sin 30° = 7 ÷ 0.5 = 14.

Rule of thumb: if the unknown is the hypotenuse, you'll be dividing, not multiplying.

If you know two sides and want the angle, use inverse trig: sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ or tan⁻¹.

Example: opposite = 3, hypotenuse = 6. Find θ.

sin θ = 3/6 = 0.5 → θ = sin⁻¹(0.5) = 30°.

Example 2: opposite = 5, adjacent = 5. tan θ = 5/5 = 1 → θ = tan⁻¹(1) = 45°.

mcqs.q: Right-angled triangle: hypotenuse = 20, angle = 30°. What is the opposite side?
If sin θ = 0.5, what is θ?

numericals.q: Right-angled triangle: opposite = 5, adjacent = 5. What is angle θ, in degrees?
numericals.hint: tan θ = O/A = 5/5 = 1. Then θ = tan⁻¹(1).

free_texts.q: To go from a sine value back to an angle, use the ____ sine function (prefix word). One word.
free_texts.hint: Written sin⁻¹ on your calculator. It 'undoes' sine.
